impl.residual_risk: The branch is PREPARE-ONLY and must not be merged as it stands: supabase/schema.sql was deliberately NOT updated for the M12 function change, because any byte change to schema.sql invalidates supabase/drift-manifest.json's sha256 and regenerating it needs `npm run drift:manifest` (Docker), and this environment has no working Docker daemon; editing schema.sql here would have left tests/drift-detection.test.ts red. Merging the migration without that mirror + manifest regeneration would itself create the live-vs-repo drift the programme exists to prevent, so the schema.sql mirror and manifest regen must land in the same change before review. Second, no SQL was executed anywhere: the M12 migrations, the guard and the Caring Contacts 0009 were verified by static contract tests and by reading the retrieval predicates (schema.sql:4176 document_labels.owner_id, :4186 document_summaries.owner_id, :4275 document_table_facts.owner_id are the only three child-owner predicates; everything else scopes by d.owner_id), not by a replay — CI's Migration replay job is the first real execution. RAG impact is genuinely nil: no predicate, comparator, ranking, ordering or selection changed; the fix only moves rows to the side of the existing public predicate where their parent document already sits. Third, M12 has a deliberate, documented behaviour consequence: once the three child owner columns are nulled during public mode, their `on delete restrict` FKs no longer block deleting that auth user, so 20260826090000's deleted-owner rollback path becomes reachable for documents that actually have labels/summaries/table facts; those rows then stay ownerless beside a status='failed' quarantined document. Table facts are excluded from retrieval by the d.status='indexed' join, and get_related_document_metadata has no status filter but is enrichment-only, fed document ids by status-filtered retrieval — that reasoning is traced, not executed. Fourth, L25 ships without the matching test case the finding asked for (tests/caring-contacts-migrations.test.ts is not in the package's owned files) and the caring-contacts db suite was NOT run: there is no local PostgreSQL server and no Docker here. Its safety rests on a source review showing both tables are written only through the audited runWrite path and the audited fixture seed, that no migration inserts into either table, and that TRUNCATE fires no row trigger. Fifth, M23 changes a script the gate-consolidation audit marks 'never touch'; the settle loop (4 reads, 30 s apart) mitigates the push-vs-apply race but adds up to 90 s to a job with a 20-minute timeout, and if the Supabase integration is ever slower than ~2 minutes the post-merge live-drift run will fail where it previously passed — which is the intended direction, but it is a new way for that job to go red. Local evidence: tests/document-corpus-access-mode.test.ts, migration-history-alignment, migration-history-guards, search-health-index-coverage, drift-detection, live-drift-workflow, supabase-schema, function-grants, caring-contacts-domain-isolation, owner-scope-guard and retrieval-access-scope all pass; `npm run check:migration-role`, `check:function-grants` and `check:owner-scope` pass; `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.typecheck.json` and eslint/prettier are clean. No provider call was made and `npm run verify:pr-local`, `check:drift`, `check:supabase-project` and the CI Migration replay job have not been run.

THE BRANCH IS PREPARE-ONLY AND MUST NOT BE MERGED AS IT STANDS. One test is deliberately red and that red is the merge block.

1) M12 mirror (this round). supabase/schema.sql now carries the 20260902090000 body of public.set_document_corpus_access_mode verbatim — the definition, its `comment on function` text, the revoke and the service_role grant — verified by a new byte-for-byte pin, not by eye. 2) supabase/drift-manifest.json was NOT regenerated, and cannot be here: it is produced only by `npm run drift:manifest`, which replays schema.sql inside the digest-pinned supabase/postgres:17.6.1 container, and `docker info` fails in this environment (confirmed). It is also not in p16's owned file list. I deliberately did NOT hand-edit it. Hand-writing the new schema_sha256 is trivially computable (d11f5789922e10b59416a8233e6ee1e654c91244f5508c30f51aa1ebf63e9faa) and would turn the offline freshness check green — but the manifest's recorded function def_hash is an md5 of Postgres's own pg_get_functiondef output, which cannot be reproduced without Postgres, so the manifest would still describe the superseded body. That is fail-OPEN: the offline gate would pass and the post-merge live-drift `check:drift` would still go red on the function. So the manifest stays stale and tests/drift-detection.test.ts is RED, printing its own remediation ("Run: npm run drift:manifest (requires Docker)"). That red is the intended fail-closed block: it makes it impossible to merge the M12 migration without regenerating the manifest, and the reviewer's required_change states this red is expected between step (1) and step (2).

3) Local evidence this round. CI's Migration replay job is the first real execution.

5) RAG impact is genuinely nil: no predicate, comparator, ranking, ordering or selection changed. The fix only moves rows to the side of the existing public predicate where their parent document already sits.

6) M12 has a documented behaviour consequence, unchanged from last round and independently confirmed by the reviewer: once the three child owner columns are nulled during public mode, their `on delete restrict` FKs no longer block deleting that auth user, so 20260826090000's deleted-owner rollback path becomes reachable for documents that have labels/summaries/table facts; those rows then stay ownerless beside a status='failed' quarantined document. Table facts are excluded from retrieval by the d.status='indexed' join; get_related_document_metadata has no status filter but is enrichment-only, fed document ids by status-filtered retrieval (src/lib/rag/rag-hydration.ts). Traced, not executed. Also: a child row that was already owner-null before a flip under an owned document is re-owned by the snapshot owner on restore (the restore matches `owner_id is null`, not "rows this activation nulled") — more restrictive, not an exposure, but the migration header's "restores exactly this set" slightly overstates the symmetry.

7) L25 ships without its required test (see findings_skipped) and the caring-contacts db suite was NOT run — no PostgreSQL server and no Docker here. Its safety rests on a source review: both tables are written only through the audited runWrite path and the audited fixture seed, no migration inserts into either table, and TRUNCATE fires no row trigger.

8) M23 changes scripts/check-migration-history-alignment.ts, which docs/audit/gate-consolidation-audit-2026-09-02.md:362 marks "LOAD-BEARING, never touch"; the package notes directed the change. Its settle loop (4 reads, 30 s apart) adds up to 90 s to a 20-minute job and, if the Supabase integration is ever slower than ~2 minutes, the post-merge live-drift run will fail where it previously passed — the intended direction, but a new way for that job to go red.
